articles.title: Bitcoin Core Tags 32.1 Final, Ending Support for 29.x Releases
articles.excerpt: Version 32.1 raises the default peer cap to 200 and adds a mempool-based fee estimator. Details of three flaws fixed in 30.0 are due in two weeks.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin Core developers published version 32.1 on GitHub on Monday, along with maintenance releases 31.2 and 30.4. The 32.1 notes say version 32.0, tagged Oct. 21, was never fully released.

The reason given is "last-minute issues," with no further detail. So 32.1 is the first build of the new major series meant for node operators. It also starts a clock: the notes say versions 29.x and older are now at "End of Life" and won't get updates.

**Nodes get room for 200 peers**

The default cap on automatic peer connections rises from 125 to 200. The extra room goes to inbound block-relay-only peers, which pass along blocks but not loose transactions. Peers that relay transactions can fill at most half of inbound slots by default. Operators who want the old limits can set `-maxconnections=125 -inboundrelaypercent=100`, the notes say.

Fee estimates change, too. The `estimatesmartfee` command now blends the existing block-based estimator with a new one that reads the mempool (the queue of unconfirmed transactions). The release also fixes a possible leak of a sender's IP address in the experimental private-broadcast feature, under certain Tor setups.

The 32.1 notes credit 128 contributors.

**Three flaws to be disclosed in two weeks**

Under the project's security policy, developers plan to disclose three medium- and high-severity vulnerabilities fixed in 30.0. The notes don't describe them yet. The 32.1 download folder on bitcoincore.org returned "not found" at 6 p.m. ET, and the site had not posted an announcement.

*In our opinion: the number worth chasing is three. Those fixes go public in about two weeks, right as 29.x stops getting patches.*

articles.title: Ripple Wins Final OCC Approval for the Trust Bank Behind RLUSD
articles.excerpt: Ripple says a federally supervised trust bank will manage reserves for its $2.5 billion RLUSD stablecoin, about 10 months after conditional approval.
articles.body_md:
RLUSD, Ripple's $2.5 billion stablecoin, is getting a federally supervised trust bank to manage its reserves. Ripple [said Monday](https://ripple.com/ripple-press/ripple-receives-final-occ-approval-to-establish-national-trust-bank/) that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted final approval to Ripple National Trust Bank.

Issuance doesn't move. Standard Custody & Trust Company, regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services, will keep minting the token. The new bank adds OCC supervision on top. It will manage the segregated reserves, act as collateral trustee for RLUSD holders and offer digital asset custody to businesses.

RLUSD was worth about $2.58 billion near midnight ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ripple-usd). Ripple said it is backed by U.S. dollar deposits, government securities and cash equivalents, with BNY as primary reserve custodian.

"For years, we've said crypto and banks work better together. Final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank is what that looks like in practice," CEO Brad Garlinghouse said in the release.

**Ten months from conditional to final**

The OCC gave [conditional approval](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-125.html) on Dec. 12, 2025, in the same batch as Circle's First National Digital Currency Bank, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets and Paxos. A trust charter isn't a full bank license. The bank can't take deposits or make loans, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-10-26-ripple-gains-final-occ-approval-rlusd-431810).

**Banks pushed back**

The Bank Policy Institute asked the OCC in an [October 2025 letter](https://bpi.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/BPI-comment-letter-re-OCC-NTB-application-re-Ripple-National-Trust-Bank-10-14-25.pdf) to reject the application. It argued that approving the charter would stretch the agency's legal authority, add new risk to the financial system and tilt the field against traditional banks that carry the full load of bank rules. That fight isn't new. The Independent Community Bankers of America has [also opposed](https://www.icba.org/web/payments/w/occ-releases-icba-opposed-national-trust-bank-chartering-rule) such charters for nonbank fintechs. We found no statement from either group on Monday's approval.

Ripple didn't say when the bank will open or what custody will cost.

*In our opinion: the date to chase now is opening day, and Ripple hasn't named one.*

articles.title: BlackRock and SBI Study Linking Tokenized Funds to a Yen Stablecoin
articles.excerpt: BlackRock signed an MOU with SBI and Startale to explore pairing tokenized money market funds with JPYSC, a $131 million yen stablecoin. No launch date was set.
articles.body_md:
BlackRock wants to see whether its tokenized money market funds can trade against a $131 million yen stablecoin. The asset manager signed a memorandum of understanding with SBI Holdings and Startale Group, the companies [announced Tuesday in Tokyo](https://www.startale.com/en/blog/blackrock-startale-sbi), Monday evening ET.

The target is JPYSC, a yen stablecoin issued through SBI Shinsei Trust Bank. Its market value was about $131.3 million near midnight ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/jpysc). BlackRock's dollar fund BUIDL was near $2.18 billion.

**How the pairing would work**

A money market fund holds short-term, low-risk debt. A tokenized version puts fund shares on a blockchain. A stablecoin can act as the cash side, so an investor could move between a fund that pays yield and a token used for payments without waiting on bank wires.

The partners will study three areas: technology, business and distribution, and regulation. SBI's [release](https://www.sbigroup.co.jp/news/2026/1027_16682.html) and Startale said the effort is open to other banks and businesses in Japan and abroad.

"The shift to onchain finance is becoming an unavoidable global trend," SBI Chairman Yoshitaka Kitao said in the announcement.

Japan set legal rules for stablecoins through amendments to its Payment Services Act, and the companies said the next step is building the infrastructure, distribution channels and regulatory frameworks that would connect tokenized assets with those coins at scale.

**What's missing**

The MOU is an agreement to explore.

It names no product, fees or timeline, and no JPYSC integration has been confirmed.

*In our opinion: an MOU is a promise to keep talking, and this one comes without a calendar. Watch who else signs up, since the door was left open for other banks.*

articles.title: Strategy Skips Bitcoin for a Week as Strive Buys $511 Million
articles.excerpt: Strategy spent $204.9 million buying back STRC preferred shares instead of bitcoin, while Strive lifted its holdings to 43,000 BTC, Monday filings show.
articles.body_md:
Strategy bought no bitcoin from Oct. 19 to Oct. 25. It spent $204.9 million buying back 2,068,459 shares of its STRC preferred stock instead, according to an [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526431146/mstr-20261026.htm) on Monday.

Strive went the other way. It bought 6,182 BTC for about $511 million between Oct. 17 and Oct. 23, its [own filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920406/000162828026067141/asst-20261026.htm) shows.

**Strategy's stack sits about 6.6% above cost**

Strategy holds roughly 848,517 bitcoin, bought for $64.02 billion at an average of about $75,446 each. Bitcoin traded near $80,400 at 11:57 a.m. ET Monday, per CoinGecko. The filing also shows no common stock sold through its at-the-market program, a plan for selling new shares into the market.

STRC is a variable-rate perpetual preferred share, so every share retired is one Strategy no longer pays dividends on. The buyback came out of "USD Cash," which fell to $242.4 million. A separate $4.83 billion reserve is set aside for dividends and debt interest. The filing doesn't say why Strategy paused its bitcoin buying.

**Strive paid more than today's price**

Strive's average price was about $82,732, roughly 2.8% above Monday's level. The purchases lifted its holdings from 36,818 to 43,000 BTC, while cash rose to $504.4 million. Strive also holds 505,000 STRC shares, valued at $50.2 million on Oct. 23.

*In our opinion: the number worth circling this week is zero, Strategy's bitcoin purchases. Strive, meanwhile, owns 505,000 of the very STRC shares Strategy was busy buying back.*

articles.title: Canada Drafts Stablecoin Rules That Ban Yield, Cap Redemption Fees
articles.excerpt: Ottawa's draft would make issuers redeem within three business days for a fee of 1% or less. Comments are due Dec. 23, with fall 2027 as the target.
articles.body_md:
Canada's Department of Finance has published draft stablecoin rules that bar issuers from paying yield and cap redemption fees at 1%. Comments are due Dec. 23 at 11:59 p.m. EST, per the [Canada Gazette](https://gazette.gc.ca/consult/consult2-eng.html).

The draft, printed in the Gazette on Oct. 24, is what Ottawa needs to switch on its Stablecoin Act. The department's stated goal is to have it in force in fall 2027.

**Who it covers**

The rules apply to issuers that are not banks or other regulated financial institutions. Those issuers would register with the Bank of Canada and hold reserves at least equal to the tokens in circulation. The department's analysis expects about five issuers, naming QCAD (Stablecorp), CADC (Loon) and Circle's USDC.

Holders would get their money back within three business days, with no minimum amount. The Gazette says market redemption fees now top out around 0.1%, but a cap that low could squeeze smaller Canadian issuers.

**Rewards yes, interest no**

Issuers couldn't pay interest for simply holding a coin, including through deals with third parties. Rewards tied to a transaction would be allowed. Supervision is paid for by issuers: those with under $500 million outstanding would pay a $25,000 base fee, and larger ones $350,000.

**Room on reserves**

Responding to industry feedback, the Gazette says, the draft sets no limits on how reserves are split among eligible assets, as long as they stay fully backed.

U.S. readers will see a familiar line. The OCC's GENIUS Act rule also bans issuers from paying interest just for [holding a payment stablecoin](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/genius-act/community-bank-fact-sheet.pdf).

articles.title: OCC Urges Community Banks to Consider Issuing Stablecoins
articles.excerpt: A new OCC fact sheet answers small banks' fears about deposit flight and yield, and invites them to apply as issuers before the GENIUS Act rule starts Jan. 18.
articles.body_md:
The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency wants community banks to consider issuing stablecoins before its GENIUS Act rule starts Jan. 18, 2027. A [fact sheet](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/genius-act/community-bank-fact-sheet.pdf) reported Monday says interested banks, or their subsidiaries, are "encouraged to consider applying" to become permitted payment stablecoin issuers.

The start date comes from [Bulletin 2026-50](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-50.html), issued Oct. 21. The stablecoin market it governs held about $303.5 billion on Monday, per DefiLlama.

**The banks' worries, in the OCC's own list**

The document is built as concerns and answers. Top of the list is deposit flight, the fear that customers move savings into stablecoins. The OCC says bank deposits can count as reserves backing a stablecoin, and that the effect on deposits is "uncertain, and estimates vary widely." It says it is watching for outflows.

On yield, the final rule dropped a proposed test (a "rebuttable presumption") for when a reward counts as banned interest. It now restates the law's ban on paying interest or yield to holders.

**Smaller issuers get longer exam cycles**

Large issuers face a full exam every 12 months. Some small issuers qualify for an 18- to 24-month cycle.

The fact sheet doesn't say how many community banks have shown interest or applied. Issuers must also tell customers that stablecoins are not FDIC-insured or backed by the government.

*In our opinion: the question worth chasing is whether any small bank files an application before Jan. 18.*

articles.title: Aviva Seeds a £50 Million Tokenized Share Class of Its Fund on XRPL
articles.excerpt: Aviva put £50 million into the new on-chain share class, lifting its two tokenized money market funds past £86 million, the firm and Ripple said.
articles.body_md:
Aviva Investors has put a tokenized share class of its Sterling Liquidity Fund, a money market fund with about £22 billion in assets, on the XRP Ledger. Aviva seeded it with £50 million ($66 million), the firm and Ripple said Monday.

It is Aviva's second fund to go on-chain, after a U.S. dollar fund in July. The two tokenized classes now hold more than £86 million ($116 million) combined, according to the [Aviva announcement](https://www.avivainvestors.com/en-gb/about/company-news/2026/10/aviva-investors-launches-tokenised-share-class-for-sterling-liquidity-fund/).

**The fund itself stays off-chain**

Aviva uses what it calls a "digital twin." The Ireland-based UCITS fund, launched in 2002, keeps running the usual way and buys short-term sterling debt. Investors' holdings are also recorded as tokens on XRPL. Bank of New York Mellon still holds the fund's assets, with digital asset custodian Komainu and tokenization platform Licuido supporting the launch.

The share class is open only to eligible investors with approved digital wallets. Aviva says it carries the same objective, risk profile and protections as the regular fund.

Ripple's Nigel Khakoo said markets "are moving to 24/7 access," in the [Ripple release](https://ripple.com/ripple-press/aviva-investors-expands-its-tokenised-offering-with-the-launch-of-a-sterling-liquidity-fund-tokenised-share-class/).

**What the release leaves out**

Aviva calls itself one of Europe's largest tokenized money market fund providers but gives no ranking data. Neither release lists the share class's fees or says how much came from outside investors beyond Aviva's own £50 million.

*In our opinion: £50 million of house money is a start. The bigger story is whether outside investors follow it in.*

*Correction (Oct. 26, 2026, 9:12 p.m. ET): An earlier version of this headline said Aviva Investors tokenized its £22 billion Sterling Liquidity Fund. Aviva put a new tokenized share class of the fund, seeded with £50 million, on the XRP Ledger. The fund itself stays off-chain.*

articles.title: Hong Kong Opens 24/7 Trading of Tokenized Money Market Funds
articles.excerpt: ChinaAMC's HKD and USD digital money funds now trade around the clock on PantherTrade, with market makers and live value estimates required by the SFC.
articles.body_md:
Hong Kong opened 24-hour secondary trading for two tokenized money market funds on Monday. The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said it is the world's first such trading of tokenized public funds.

The two products are ChinaAMC's HKD and USD Digital Money Market Funds. Their token shares now trade on PantherTrade, an SFC-licensed crypto exchange, according to a [ChinaAMC shareholder notice](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/1023/2026102301619.pdf) filed with HKEX on Oct. 23. Buying from and redeeming with the fund itself stays open.

For crypto traders, the change is about timing. A tokenized fund share can now be sold on a Saturday night instead of waiting for the fund's next dealing day.

**Market makers and a 15-second price check**

The SFC wrote the rules in an [April 20 circular](https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/doc?refNo=26EC23). It asks fund managers to arrange at least one market maker per fund, with three months' notice before one quits. It also requires the licensed exchange to post an indicative net asset value (a live estimate of what each share is worth), [typically updated at least every 15 seconds](https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/doc?refNo=26EC23), and warn buyers when a trade price strays too far from it.

The same circular tells platforms to warn clients about very thin trading and large premiums or discounts outside Hong Kong market hours and on weekends.

"We will continue to strengthen Hong Kong's position as a pioneer in tokenization by facilitating responsible innovation while safeguarding investors," Elisa Ng, the SFC's executive director of investment products, said, as quoted by [The Standard](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/346511/SFC-approves-worlds-first-secondary-trading-of-tokenized-public-funds).

The regulator said it will watch the first trades before deciding whether to let other kinds of funds in.

*In our opinion: the number to chase is the price gap on the first weekend. A money fund trading close to its own value at 3 a.m. on a Sunday would say more than any launch release.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Slips Back Below $80,000 as Fed Decision Nears
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin was at $79,429 late Sunday, down 1.7% on the day and 3.9% on the week, while ether lost 5% over seven days ahead of the Fed's Oct. 28 decision.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell back below $80,000 late Sunday and was at $79,429 at 11:59 p.m. ET, down 1.7% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Earlier in the day it touched $80,875. That's two weekend trips under $80,000.

That leaves it a few hundred dollars above Saturday's low. Coinbase's bitcoin-dollar market bottomed at $79,107 on Saturday (UTC) and at $79,255 over the past 24 hours, according to [Coinbase Exchange market data](https://api.exchange.coinbase.com/products/BTC-USD/stats). Over seven days, bitcoin is down 3.9%, per CoinGecko.

**Ether fell harder**

Ether was near $2,301, down 2.5% on the day and 5% on the week, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum). On Coinbase, the [ETH-USD market](https://api.exchange.coinbase.com/products/ETH-USD/stats) dipped to $2,290 before bouncing slightly.

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 50, labeled neutral, down from 54 a day earlier, per [Alternative.me](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/).

**Fed decision lands Wednesday**

The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee meets Tuesday and Wednesday, Oct. 27-28, according to the [Fed's meeting calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm). Its decision on borrowing costs is due at the end of the meeting. Rates matter here because they set what traders pay to borrow and hold positions.

*In our opinion: $80,000 makes a tidy headline, but Wednesday's Fed statement is the line worth chasing this week. We'll be reading every word.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: CoinDCX Confirms $16 Million Loss Days After Saying It Wasn't Breached
articles.excerpt: India's CoinDCX says 15.99 million USDT left retired wallets after a deposit sweep failed. It says it covered the loss and customer balances are intact.
articles.body_md:
CoinDCX says it lost 15.99 million USDT, about $16 million, from old wallets it retired after a 2025 security incident. The Indian exchange put a number on it in a [blog post](https://coindcx.com/blog/coindcx-news/on-chain-wallet-activity-update-21-oct-2026) early Sunday and said the company absorbed the loss.

Wednesday's message was different. Hours after the funds moved, co-founder and CEO Sumit Gupta [wrote on X](https://x.com/smtgpt/status/2113181173480607981) that "CoinDCX wallets are not breached" and asked people not to spread rumours.

**A failed sweep left deposits in a retired address**

CoinDCX said it spotted unusual activity on Oct. 21. The next day, blockchain data and user reports showed money leaving its deprecated wallet setup, which the exchange said "had unknown vulnerabilities."

Some users had kept sending deposits to those old addresses. CoinDCX credits those deposits to customer accounts right away, and a separate service later sweeps the coins into its main wallet. That service "had failed for a particular period," the post said, so the USDT piled up where it could be taken.

On-chain investigator ZachXBT had publicly challenged the exchange's first account, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-25-coindcx-confirms-16-million-loss-from-retired-wallets-days-after-ceo-called-breach-reports-a-false-alarm-431617).

**What customers are told**

CoinDCX said deposit balances are fully accounted for, customer funds sit in segregated cold wallets, and trading, deposits and withdrawals ran without a pause. "We could have been more proactive," it wrote.

The exchange now tells users to check the current deposit address in its app before every transfer.

**In our opinion:** Retired deposit addresses are a quiet risk at any exchange. Warning users off them helps, but the backend that watches them has to keep working too.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Says It Downed 10 Houthi Missiles Aimed at Its South
articles.excerpt: Riyadh's main airport reopened Sunday even as drones and missiles flew at the capital. Brent ended last week at $116.72, its highest settle since April.
articles.body_md:
Saudi air defenses shot down 10 ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis at the kingdom's south on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said. More drones and a ballistic missile were stopped on their way to Riyadh.

The oil link is direct. The Houthis said their targets included Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu, and Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel on Friday, its highest close since April 29, per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/25/saudi-arabia-houthi-missile-drone-interceptions.html). Pricier oil feeds inflation worries, and that makes rate cuts harder to argue for in a Fed week.

**Shrapnel fell in Mecca province**

Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki also reported a cruise missile intercepted near Khamis Mushait, according to the Saudi Press Agency as cited by CNBC. Saudi Civil Defence said debris from two intercepted missiles landed in Jeddah, Taif and other parts of Mecca province, [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/25/saudi-air-defences-intercept-houthi-barrage-near-mecca) reported.

The Houthis said on Telegram they carried out seven operations against airports, energy sites and military bases. They denied aiming at Muslim holy sites. Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to CNBC.

**The airport reopened anyway**

King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resumed flights Sunday, with Terminal 2 for international routes and Terminal 1 for domestic ones. It had shut after an Oct. 10 strike that killed 13 people.

Bitcoin barely reacted. It traded near $80,580 at 11:55 a.m. ET, up 1.3% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Oil futures reopen Sunday evening, and the Fed announces its decision Oct. 28, per its official calendar.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: 109 Israeli Economists Slam Netanyahu's Crypto Sanctions Plan
articles.excerpt: Two Nobel laureates and a former Bank of Israel governor signed the letter, which calls crypto a tool of criminal groups and says it won't shield Israel from sanctions.
articles.body_md:
A letter signed by 109 Israeli economists, executives and former officials says Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's idea of using crypto to get around banking sanctions would do nothing to protect the economy. It was published Sunday.

This is the second big rebuke in two days. The Bank of Israel said Saturday that crypto cannot be a route around sanctions. Now a long list of the country's best-known economists has piled on.

**Who signed**

The signers include Joel Mokyr, the 2025 Nobel laureate in economics, and Aaron Ciechanover, a Nobel laureate in chemistry, according to [Ynetnews](https://www.ynetnews.com/business/article/syqpcmjhgl) and [CTech by Calcalist](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/rly4kiczs). Former Bank of Israel governor Jacob Frenkel, four former Finance Ministry directors-general and two former bank supervisors also signed, along with Check Point co-founder Marius Nacht.

The letter warns that broad banking sanctions would cause "irreversible damage." It says Israelis could lose the use of credit cards and that exporters and the tech sector could not function. It calls crypto workarounds a method associated with criminal organizations.

**Netanyahu hasn't dropped it**

Netanyahu raised the idea Friday on an Israeli economic TV channel, saying the country should prepare an alternative system to bypass banking sanctions. On Saturday he said he takes the central bank's objections into account but does what he thinks is right, [Middle East Eye](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/diplomatic-financial-isolation-netanyahu-crypto-plan-bypass-sanctions-draws-rebuke) reported. Neither Ynetnews nor CTech reported a response from his office to the letter.

Netanyahu framed banking sanctions as a risk, not a reality. The UK and 11 other countries have so far targeted trade in goods from West Bank settlements, Middle East Eye reported.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Zcash Jumps 6% to $1,210 as Bitcoin and Ether Take Sunday Slow
articles.excerpt: ZEC is up 8.5% on the week and holds the No. 10 spot by market value, though it is still down 24% over 30 days, CoinGecko data show.
articles.body_md:
Zcash's ZEC token rose 6.2% in 24 hours to about $1,210 at 11:55 a.m. ET on Sunday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/zcash). Bitcoin managed 1.3%. Ether did 2%.

That makes the privacy coin the busiest name in the top 10 on a quiet weekend. Its market value sits near $20.6 billion, good for the No. 10 spot on CoinGecko's ranking.

**A better week, a rough month**

ZEC traded between $1,137 and $1,223 over the past day and is up 8.5% over seven days. The 30-day view is less cheerful: it is still down about 24%, which is the kind of number that makes a 6% Sunday look like a down payment.

**The big two stayed put**

Bitcoin traded near $80,580, up 1.3% in 24 hours but down 1.1% on the week, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Ether sat near $2,342, up 2% on the day and down 13% over 30 days, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

No single headline explains Sunday's ZEC move, and CoinGecko's numbers show price, not motive. Weekend trading is often thin, so moves can be bigger than the news behind them.

*In our opinion: Zcash is built to keep things private, and on Sunday it kept its reasons to itself, too.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: South Korea Leans Toward a Fourth Delay of Its 22% Crypto Tax
articles.excerpt: Seoul is weighing another delay to its tax on crypto gains, citing gaps in overseas exchange data. A ruling-party bill would push the start to 2029.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's presidential office is leaning toward pushing back its crypto income tax a fourth time, Korean outlets reported Sunday, citing ruling-party sources. The 22% tax is set to start Jan. 1, 2027.

Officially, nothing is settled. The presidential office said a delay is "under review" and that no decision has been made, [Yonhap](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/MYH20261025011500038) reported.

For Korean traders the stakes are simple. The tax would take 22%, including local income tax, of yearly crypto gains above a 2.5 million won deduction, according to [The Asia Business Daily](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026102517522309926) and [Financial News](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202610251416295006).

**Korea's crypto tax has been "next year" since 2022**

It was first due to start in 2022 and has been delayed three times since. The third date didn't stick either.

**Foreign exchanges are the sticking point**

The main worry is data from overseas platforms. The U.S. isn't expected to join the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, a deal for tax authorities to swap crypto account data, until 2029, [Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/politics/2026/10/25/presidential-office-decides-to-delay-crypto-tax-again) and The Asia Business Daily reported. Officials fear the tax would land mostly on people who trade on domestic exchanges.

Both big parties want more time. Democratic Party lawmaker Park Min-gyu has filed a bill that would move the start to 2029, and the opposition People Power Party also backs a delay, both outlets reported. A final call is expected after talks between the government and the ruling party.

*In our opinion: a tax first scheduled for 2022 may now show up in 2029. Korean investors have heard "next year" before.*

articles.title: Iran Says It Shot Down a U.S. Drone Over Bandar Abbas
articles.excerpt: Iran's army says its air defenses downed a U.S. LUCAS attack drone near the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. officials had not responded, and bitcoin held near $80,240.
articles.body_md:
Iran's army said its air defenses shot down a U.S. drone over the port city of Bandar Abbas on Sunday, according to a [Reuters report carried by Arab News](https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/iranian-army-says-it-shot-down-us-drone-over-bandar-abbas-tasnim-reports-3008153) that cited the semi-official Tasnim agency. No one outside Iran has confirmed it.

Bandar Abbas sits on the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow route tankers use to carry Gulf crude to the world. Higher oil feeds inflation, and inflation is what the Federal Reserve weighs when it meets Oct. 27-28, per the [Fed's calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

**Tehran named the drone type**

The army's public relations office said a "U.S. Lucas drone" was destroyed by its integrated air defense network, Iran's [Mehr News Agency](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/248893/Iran-army-downs-US-Lucas-drone-over-Bandar-Abbas) reported. [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610253096) carried the same claim.

LUCAS is a low-cost, one-way attack drone that U.S. Central Command fields in the Middle East, according to [CENTCOM](https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/igphoto/2003834256/) and [DefenseScoop](https://defensescoop.com/2026/08/13/centcom-creates-multinational-attack-drone-task-force/).

**No word from Washington**

U.S. officials had not publicly responded to the claim in the reports reviewed by 6 a.m. ET. Iran gave no details on the drone's mission or any wreckage.

Crypto barely moved. Bitcoin traded near $80,240 at 6:01 a.m. ET, down 0.4% in 24 hours, and ether was near $2,325, down 1.7%, per CoinGecko ([BTC](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), [ETH](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum)).

*In our opinion: one side's account of a shoot-down is a claim, not a confirmed event. The other side hasn't spoken yet.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk
